beats.text: Crossing a river used to mean getting wet, or worse.
The first bridges were just fallen logs, laid across a stream.
Later, people stacked stones and laid flat slabs on top.
The Romans mastered the stone arch. Its curve pushes the weight down into the ground, and some still stand after two thousand years.
In the mountains, the Inca wove rope bridges from grass, across deep gorges.
In 1779, England built the first iron bridge.
Steel trusses then carried heavy trains across wide rivers.
Suspension bridges hang the road from huge cables, like the Golden Gate in 1937.
Today, cable-stayed bridges run cables straight from tall towers, spanning over a kilometer.
Follow to see how everything evolved.
